questions.text: What report concerning Jerusalem did Hanani bring unto Nehemiah in Shushan the palace?

options.text: The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and the gates are burned with fire
The king of Persia purposed to destroy the altar of burnt offerings
The priests in Jerusalem have turned away to worship strange gods
The armies of the Arabians have laid siege unto the cities of Judah

questions.text: Unto what word commanded to Moses did Nehemiah appeal in his prayer?

options.text: That God would take away all the horses and chariots from the enemies
If ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments, yet will I gather you
That no stranger shall ever enter into the gates of the sanctuary
That the children of Israel should never be brought under tribute

questions.text: What office of trust did Nehemiah hold in Shushan the palace?

options.text: He was chief captain over the royal garrison in the palace
He was treasurer over the royal storehouses of the kingdom
He was the king's cupbearer unto king Artaxerxes in Shushan
He was chief ambassador unto the governors of the provinces

questions.text: What did Nehemiah do when the king said unto him: For what dost thou make request?

options.text: He called for his brethren that were come out of the captivity
He demanded instant letters from the king unto all the governors
He bowed himself before the throne desiring counsel for one day
He prayed to the God of heaven before he made answer to the king

questions.text: How did Nehemiah view the broken walls of Jerusalem after he arrived?

options.text: Secretly by night upon a beast with a few men, telling no man of it
With a company of armed horsemen by day in presence of the rulers
He went up to the tower of Hananeel looking down upon the ruins
He sent out strange spies from Samaria to bring him word thereof

questions.text: How did Nehemiah answer the scorn of Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem?

options.text: We have royal soldiers from the king who shall smite you with sword
The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise
We will give you tribute of silver if ye suffer us to build in peace
King Artaxerxes will send his mighty captains to carry you captive

questions.text: Who rose up and builded the sheep gate of the city of Jerusalem?

options.text: The goldsmiths and apothecaries of the city of Jerusalem
The rulers of the half part of the province with servants
Eliashib the high priest with his brethren the priests
The men of Jericho together with the rulers of Mizpah

questions.text: Which company refused haughtily to put their necks to the work of the LORD?

options.text: The merchants who would not leave their wares in the streets
The men of war who refused to lay down their spears and shields
The priests of the sons of Harim who remained within the court
The nobles of the Tekoites who put not their necks to the work

questions.text: What notable order was observed in repairing the wall over against dwellings?

options.text: Many repaired the wall every one over against his own house
The portions of the wall were parted daily by casting of lots
Only strange hired masons were suffered to set up the stones
The Levites erected all the gates while people carried away rubbish

questions.text: With what mocking words did Tobiah the Ammonite despise the wall of Jerusalem?

options.text: These feeble stones will moulder away at the first winter rain!
If a fox go up, he shall even break down their stone wall!
The builders will faint with hunger before they set up the doors!
A single horse of battle will cast down their weak foundations!

questions.text: What defence did the builders make when the adversaries conspired to fight against them?

options.text: They sent a great sum of silver from the temple to satisfy Sanballat
They sent swift messengers unto Artaxerxes requiring a band of horsemen
They made prayer unto their God, and set a watch against them day and night
They commanded all the people to leave the building and hide themselves

questions.text: How did they which laded and they that bare burdens labour under the threat of war?

options.text: They laboured only by night under the thick shadow of darkness
They made great palisades of timber behind which they wrought
They suffered only the mighty men to build, while women watched
With one of his hands he wrought, and with the other held a weapon

questions.text: What great cry of the poor people and their wives came before Nehemiah?

options.text: They mortgaged lands and brought children into bondage for corn
The priests refused to offer sacrifice for them without money
Men of Tyre took away their cattle out of the pastures by force
The governor of the province had seized their vineyards for king

questions.text: With what symbolic act did Nehemiah confirm the oath against the usurers?

options.text: He brake an earthen pot in pieces before all the congregation
He shook his lap: So God shake out every man from his house
He cast their bills of debt into the burning fire of the altar
He caused the extortioners to be bound thirty days at the gate

questions.text: What self-denial did Nehemiah show during his twelve years of government?

options.text: He did eat only coarse barley bread and drank water of the brook
He sold all his garments and lay upon the dust in the court
He required not the bread of the governor, nor bought any land
He walked without armed guards among the people day and night

questions.text: What answer sent Nehemiah when Sanballat sent to meet him in the plain of Ono?

options.text: I will come with an hundred soldiers to treat with thee of peace
Send thy terms in writing unto the sheep gate of the holy city
The king of Persia hath forbidden me all converse with strangers
I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down: why cease?

questions.text: What answered Nehemiah when Shemaiah counselled him to shut himself in the temple?

options.text: Should such a man as I flee? I will not go into the temple!
I have not the garments of the priests to stand in the house
The doors of the sanctuary are too weak against the enemies
The high priest hath forbidden me to enter into the holy place

questions.text: In how many days was the wall of Jerusalem finished by the builders?

options.text: In forty days upon the first day of the seventh month of the year
In fifty and two days, in the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul
In seven weeks until the coming of the royal letters from Shushan
In an hundred and twenty days before the feast of the passover

questions.text: Whom did Nehemiah put in charge over Jerusalem, and for what reason?

options.text: His nephew Bilshan because he had great riches and many friends
The rulers of Samaria to maintain peace with neighbouring lands
Hananiah the ruler of the palace: for he was a faithful man, fearing God
Eliashib the priest, that the law might govern all the affairs

questions.text: What condition was in the city of Jerusalem when the wall was builded?

options.text: There was no fountain of water, for all wells were stopped up
The walls were too low to defend the people against ladders of war
There was great lack of bread and cattle, so that people fainted
The city was large and great: but the people were few, houses not builded

questions.text: What did Nehemiah when God put into his heart to number the congregation?

options.text: He gathered nobles, rulers, and people, that they might be reckoned
He commanded all the people to depart from the city unto fields
He gathered a heavy tribute upon every household to pay debt
He numbered the men of war to go forth to battle with Sanballat

questions.text: How did all the people answer when Ezra opened the book of the law in their sight?

options.text: They cried aloud for a sign from heaven to confirm the words
All the people stood up, answered 'Amen, Amen', and bowed heads
They held their peace in great fear and departed out of the place
The rulers murmured aloud against the strict statutes of the law

questions.text: What did the Levites do as Ezra read out of the book in the law of God?

options.text: They collected the tithes and gifts of silver from the people
They wrote the names of all the families upon rolls of skin
They read distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused to understand
They sang the songs of David with psalteries between chapters

questions.text: With what comfortable words were the weeping people comforted at the law?

options.text: Weep not, for all your adversaries are fled into the desert!
The LORD will make you rich and honourable above all heathen!
The fenced walls stand sure and no enemy shall prevail today!
Mourn not, nor weep; for the joy of the LORD is your strength!

questions.text: In what manner were the children of Israel assembled in the twenty and fourth day?

options.text: With fasting, and with sackclothes, and earth upon them in prayer
In beautiful garments of linen with harps and joyous dancing
In harness of war with drawn swords before the holy sanctuary
In solemn silence standing round about the ark upon mount Zion

questions.text: What gracious nature of God is praised in the solemn prayer of the Levites?

options.text: That He consumeth the ungodly nations immediately in His wrath
Thou art a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, of great kindness
That He regardeth only the burnt offerings of oxen and lambs
That He taketh away the golden crowns from the princes of earth

questions.text: How did the Levites describe the present condition of the people under Persia?

options.text: Behold, we are increased in riches and dominion above our fathers
The LORD hath utterly forsaken His heritage unto the heathen
Behold, we are servants this day in the land that thou gavest us
We dwell in glorious liberty owing no tribute unto any monarch

questions.text: What solemn covenant did the people make concerning the holy sabbath day?

options.text: Never to drink wine nor eat flesh within the gates of the city
To break all trade with strange merchants upon the great sea
To withhold all royal tribute from the king of Persia in Shushan
If the people of the land bring ware on sabbath, not to buy it

questions.text: With what solemn vow did the people conclude their covenant for the sanctuary?

options.text: And we will not forsake the house of our God!
We will overlay the chambers of the temple with gold of Ophir!
No uncircumcised stranger shall ever pass the threshold of house!
We vow to offer a thousand sheep for a daily burnt offering!

questions.text: What ordinance did the people make to charge themselves yearly for the temple?

options.text: A whole shekel of gold from every man of war in the province
The third part of a shekel for the service of the house of God
A tenth of all the corn for the table of the Persian governor
Two fat rams out of every household for the solemn passover

questions.explanation: The congregation charged themselves yearly with the third part of a shekel (approx. 3.8 g of silver) for the temple service [ref:Nehemiah 10:32].

questions.text: How was it determined who should dwell in Jerusalem, the holy city?

options.text: They chose only the wealthiest households with their servants
Volunteers out of the tribe of Levi were alone compelled
They cast lots, to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem
King Artaxerxes appointed the dwellers by an imperial decree

questions.text: What honour was given unto those that offered themselves to dwell at Jerusalem?

options.text: They received a double portion of land throughout all Judah
The people blessed all the men, that willingly offered themselves
They were released for ever from all tribute and royal service
They received crowns of gold from the governor of the palace

questions.text: What sacred title is given unto the city of Jerusalem in the eleventh chapter?

options.text: The strong fortress of the south against all enemies
The glorious crown of kingdoms bordering wilderness
The refuge of all princes of the realms of Persia
The holy city unto the LORD God of the covenant

questions.text: How was the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem celebrated with gladness?

options.text: Two great companies of them that gave thanks went upon the wall
They burned ten thousand censers of incense upon the corner towers
All the gates remained shut seven days for a solemn fast of soul
The men of war made a tournament of battle upon the battlements

questions.text: How great was the joy of the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem?

options.text: It was heard only within the narrow courts of the sanctuary
The joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar off round about
Unto the palace of Shushan in the far country of Persia
Unto the river Euphrates and the ancient gates of Babylon

questions.text: Who went before the first company of them that gave thanks upon the wall?

options.text: Royal heralds with silver trumpets from the palace
The valiant men of war bearing the shields of gold
Ezra the scribe went before them with the singers
Eliashib the high priest with the golden vessels

questions.text: What evil did Nehemiah discover in the house of God when he came to Jerusalem?

options.text: They had used the brazen altar for strange drink offerings
The Levites had sold the timber of the sanctuary to merchants
Goldsmiths were melting down the sacred bowls for trade
Eliashib had prepared for Tobiah a great chamber in court

questions.text: How did Nehemiah cleanse the chamber that had been prepared for Tobiah?

options.text: He cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of chamber
He treated with Tobiah for an annual rent of the chamber
He caused Eliashib the priest to be put to death at the gate
He builded up the door thereof with stones that none enter

questions.text: With what prayer does Nehemiah conclude the record of his book?

options.text: O LORD, consume all the heathen nations in thy wrath!
Remember me, O my God, for good according to mercy!
May the walls of Jerusalem stand strong for evermore!
Behold, all my work is finished before thine eyes!
